sections.title: The Grain Offering
observations: The grain offering, or meal offering, is a significant aspect of the sacrificial system in Leviticus. It represents a gift of gratitude and dedication to God, acknowledging His provision and sovereignty.
Unlike the burnt offering, which is wholly consumed, the grain offering is partially given to the priests, symbolizing the sharing of God's blessings with His servants.

The offering is to be made of fine flour, indicating the quality and purity expected in offerings to God. The inclusion of oil and frankincense enhances the offering, symbolizing the richness of the worshiper’s devotion.

sections.title: Preparation and Presentation
observations: The preparation of the grain offering involves mixing the flour with oil and frankincense, which signifies the importance of preparation in worship. It teaches us that our offerings to God should be made with care and intentionality.
The act of presenting the offering before the Lord emphasizes the need for a personal relationship with God. Worship is not merely a ritual but an act of devotion and submission to His will.

sections.title: The Role of the Priests
observations: The priests play a crucial role in the offering process, as they are the mediators between God and the people. This foreshadows the ultimate priesthood of Christ, who mediates a new covenant.
The portion of the offering that is given to the priests serves as their sustenance, highlighting the importance of supporting those who serve in ministry.

importantVerses.commentary: The introduction of the grain offering sets the stage for understanding the various types of offerings in the sacrificial system, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and dedication to God.
The requirement to season every grain offering with salt signifies the enduring nature of God's covenant and the necessity of purity in our offerings.

questions: What does the grain offering teach us about our attitude towards God and His provisions?
How can we apply the principles of preparation and presentation in our own worship today?
In what ways does the role of the priests in the Old Testament foreshadow the work of Christ as our High Priest?
